name: reviewdog
gap_vs_coprogrammer: Does not reason about branch intent or semantic integration.
notes: Candidate inspiration for digest finding reporters.

name: Danger JS
gap_vs_coprogrammer: Rules run around a PR but do not digest branch intent or rebuild patches.
notes: Useful reference for future scriptable policy hooks.

name: Sourcegraph Batch Changes
gap_vs_coprogrammer: Optimizes large-scale planned changes, not multi-agent branch digestion.
notes: Strong reference for Integration Patch Bot records and reconciliation.

name: OpenRewrite
gap_vs_coprogrammer: Transforms code according to recipes but does not decide branch intent or integration policy.
notes: Possible deterministic patch primitive for future semantic integration.

name: Comby
gap_vs_coprogrammer: Patch primitive only; no branch digestion or policy layer.
notes: Candidate deterministic transformation backend.

name: Prow Tide
gap_vs_coprogrammer: Coordinates merging after review; does not extract or preserve branch insights.
notes: Reference for queue status, not for semantic integration.

name: MergePilot
gap_vs_coprogrammer: Appears conflict-resolution oriented; protocol/digest/record layer remains CoProgrammer differentiation.
notes: Track closely.

name: Paperclip
gap_vs_coprogrammer: Paperclip manages broad AI labor and AI-run companies. CoProgrammer should specialize in repository state, branch digestion, semantic integration, contract risk, and integration records.
notes: Strongest current reference for Manager Plane direction. Track closely but keep CoProgrammer software-integration-specific.

name: OpenReview
gap_vs_coprogrammer: Reviews submitted PRs but does not manage leases, branch digestion, or semantic patch reconstruction.
notes: Reference for future GitHub App packaging.

name: GitWand
gap_vs_coprogrammer: Works after conflicts appear; does not preserve branch intent or manage integration decisions.
notes: Borrow confidence taxonomy for integration risk.

name: Pullfrog
gap_vs_coprogrammer: General agent execution layer; CoProgrammer should specialize in Manager Plane state and integration artifacts.
notes: Useful for command UX and GitHub-native workflow.

name: Renovate
gap_vs_coprogrammer: Domain-specific dependency automation; does not manage multi-agent coding integration.
notes: Borrow dashboard issue and policy configuration patterns.

name: Probot
gap_vs_coprogrammer: Framework only; CoProgrammer still owns semantic integration protocol.
notes: Candidate implementation framework if moving beyond GitHub Actions.

name: Grit
gap_vs_coprogrammer: Transformation layer; not a Manager Plane or semantic integration governance system.
notes: Candidate deterministic patch primitive.

name: CodeRabbit
gap_vs_coprogrammer: Reviews PRs as submitted; does not own branch-intent digestion or integration records.
notes: Commercial adjacent tool; integrate signals rather than replace.

name: GitHub Copilot Code Review
gap_vs_coprogrammer: Not open source and not a Manager Plane; does not reconstruct minimal semantic patches.
notes: Reference for native UX expectations.

name: bors-ng
gap_vs_coprogrammer: Merge queue pattern only; does not digest branch intent or manage agent state.
notes: Historical reference for integration branch discipline.

name: GitHub Merge Queue
useful_ideas: Validate queued PRs against latest target branch
Use queue as final safety gate
gap_vs_coprogrammer: Validates final commit state but does not choose which parts of noisy AI branches should survive.
notes: CoProgrammer should delegate final merge ordering to it when available.

name: GitLab Merge Trains
gap_vs_coprogrammer: Coordinates merge order and pipelines, not branch-intent extraction or semantic patch rebuilding.
notes: Support as downstream merge gate in GitLab environments.

name: SemanticMerge
useful_ideas: Differentiate text conflict from structural conflict
gap_vs_coprogrammer: Code-shape oriented; does not manage branch intent, human decisions, or integration records.
notes: Useful conceptual reference for conflict classification.

name: Mergify
gap_vs_coprogrammer: Merge automation only; no Manager Plane or branch digest semantics.
notes: Integrate as downstream queue where teams already use it.

name: Graphite Merge Queue
gap_vs_coprogrammer: Optimizes PR flow but does not digest agent branches or rebuild minimal patches.
notes: Reference for stacked PR teams.

name: DevNous
useful_ideas: Translate unstructured team dialogue into structured governance artifacts
gap_vs_coprogrammer: Project-management oriented; CoProgrammer needs repository-native state such as leases, contracts, digests, and integration records.
notes: Useful for manager-as-governance framing, especially turning chat into durable project state.

name: Failed Agentic Pull Requests Study
useful_ideas: Use failed PR data to validate taxonomy
Connect reviewer outcomes to digest fields
Ground product decisions in empirical evidence
gap_vs_coprogrammer: Evidence source only; not a product or component.
notes: Use in Track B to validate failure taxonomy.

name: OpenHands
gap_vs_coprogrammer: Agent runtime and platform; does not define a repository integration manager with branch digestion, leases, or decision records.
notes: Integrate or interoperate as an agent runtime rather than competing with it.

name: SWE-agent
useful_ideas: Agent-computer interface as a first-class design problem
Repository navigation and edit affordances for agents
Task performance depends on interface design
gap_vs_coprogrammer: Optimizes a single agent's interface to software tools; CoProgrammer coordinates many agents and the integration path back to main.
notes: Use as evidence that agents need purpose-built interfaces, then extend the idea to team-level interfaces.

name: OpenAI Codex Cloud Agent
useful_ideas: Terminal/test evidence attached to task results
gap_vs_coprogrammer: Provides agent execution and task artifacts, but not a cross-agent semantic integration manager or durable lease/decision board.
notes: Strong evidence that teams will run many background coding tasks in parallel and need coordination state above the agent runtime.

name: GitHub Copilot Cloud Agent
useful_ideas: Custom agents for specialized task types
REST API surface for starting and managing tasks
gap_vs_coprogrammer: Creates and iterates PRs inside GitHub; does not digest multiple agent branches into minimal integration patches under project policy.
notes: Treat as a likely upstream agent producer. CoProgrammer should consume its PRs, logs, and branch outputs.

name: AGENTS.md
useful_ideas: Predictable repository-level instructions for coding agents
Portable starting point across agent tools
gap_vs_coprogrammer: Instruction files guide agent behavior but do not store live state, leases, decisions, contract board entries, or integration records.
notes: CoProgrammer should generate or validate minimal AGENTS.md guidance, but avoid turning policy into a long prompt file.

name: Model Context Protocol
useful_ideas: Expose Manager Plane state as tools/resources
Use elicitation for human decisions later
gap_vs_coprogrammer: MCP standardizes context/tool access; it does not define software integration objects or merge policy.
notes: Future CoProgrammer Manager should likely expose an MCP server.

name: Agent2Agent Protocol
useful_ideas: Potential future bridge between Manager Plane and external agent runtimes
gap_vs_coprogrammer: Agent-to-agent communication does not solve repository-specific coordination, branch digestion, or semantic integration.
notes: CoProgrammer should not become an A2A competitor; it can become a software-state service used through A2A.

name: Centralized Asynchronous Isolated Delegation
useful_ideas: Branch-and-merge as a core multi-agent mechanism
gap_vs_coprogrammer: Research paradigm; CoProgrammer can operationalize it as leases, event logs, decision queues, and integration records.
notes: This is the closest research match to the Manager Plane direction.

name: Agentic PR Merge/Rejection Study
useful_ideas: Measure review interactions, not only merge outcome
Capture decision rationale as first-class evidence
Separate agent failure from workflow constraints
gap_vs_coprogrammer: Evidence source only; reinforces need for decision records and integration history.
notes: Use to justify decision records and reviewer-interaction metrics in Track B.

name: Continue
gap_vs_coprogrammer: Focuses on AI checks and coding assistance; CoProgrammer owns semantic integration state and decision records.
notes: High-priority reference for policy-as-code and CI gates.

name: Cline
gap_vs_coprogrammer: Agent runtime and UX; does not maintain cross-agent leases, contract board, or integration records.
notes: Borrow human-in-the-loop execution UX.

name: aider
gap_vs_coprogrammer: Optimizes a single agent pair-programming loop; CoProgrammer coordinates multiple branch outputs and integration decisions.
notes: Strong reference for patch ergonomics and Git workflow.

name: opencode
gap_vs_coprogrammer: Runtime layer; CoProgrammer should consume its branches and evidence rather than duplicate it.
notes: High-star runtime reference for CLI ergonomics.

name: Gemini CLI
gap_vs_coprogrammer: Agent runtime; does not define repository semantic integration policy.
notes: Reference for task logs and terminal evidence.

name: LangGraph
gap_vs_coprogrammer: General workflow framework; CoProgrammer still defines software-specific objects and policies.
notes: Potential future substrate for Manager workflows.

name: LiteLLM
gap_vs_coprogrammer: Model infrastructure only; CoProgrammer defines risk-based routing policy and integration artifacts.
notes: Relevant to model routing and simple-work model policy.

name: Semgrep
gap_vs_coprogrammer: Validation engine; does not manage branch intent, leases, or integration records.
notes: Candidate validation primitive.

name: ast-grep
gap_vs_coprogrammer: Patch primitive only; CoProgrammer decides when and why to apply it.
notes: High-priority deterministic patch primitive.

name: tree-sitter
gap_vs_coprogrammer: Parser infrastructure; CoProgrammer still needs integration semantics and policy.
notes: Potential foundation for semantic diff and symbol-aware conflict forecast.

name: Coder
useful_ideas: Secure workspaces for developers and agents
gap_vs_coprogrammer: Workspace platform; CoProgrammer coordinates software integration state above the workspace.
notes: Reference for isolated agent workspace deployment.
